newsitem.title: UK: British aluminium can recycling at record levels.
newsitem.headline: British aluminium can recycling at record levels.

text.p: Aluminium can recycling has reached an all-time high in the U.K. for the eighth successive year, the Aluminium Can Recycling Association (ACRA) said in a release.
In 1996 1.5 billion aluminium cans (23,849 tonnes) were calculated as being collected for recycling by the UK public, equating to a recycling rate of 31 percent.
The aluminium industry set up its UK can recycling programme in 1989, since when it has invested 60 million stg in its development.
There are now 380 'Cash for Cans' centres plus can collection vans calling at over 270 collection sites, mainly supermarket car parks, where cash is paid to customers for their aluminium empties.
"We are delighted with the results, the continued support from both members of the public and the trade has been tremendous," said ACRAs National Manager, Alex Griffin.
Aluminium drinks cans are infinitely recyclable, being made back into new drinks cans or other high quality products, time and again with no loss of quality.
Massive energy savings of up to 95 percent are achieved through recycling, and the mining of bauxite for primary production is avoided.
